name: SQL Injection Incident Response Runbook
immediate_actions: Verify whether the application returned database errors (HTTP 500) or database responses.
Check database query audit logs to determine if queries returned unauthorized rows or modified tables.
Block the attacking source IP address at the firewall/WAF.
Notify the development team to patch the vulnerable endpoint with prepared statements.

name: Brute Force and Credential Spray Runbook
immediate_actions: Identify all usernames targeted by the attacking IP.
Verify whether any subsequent login from the attacking IP succeeded.
If a login succeeded: immediately terminate active user sessions and trigger a forced password reset.
Add the offending IP address to the temporary blocklist (Fail2Ban/firewall).

name: Compromised Account Response Runbook
immediate_actions: Immediately revoke all active sessions and tokens for the compromised account.
Trigger an emergency password reset and enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).
Isolate the host or workstation where the administrative session was established to prevent lateral movement.
Block the offending source IP address at the perimeter firewall and WAF.

name: Path Traversal and LFI Runbook
immediate_actions: Check the HTTP response status and byte size to determine if sensitive files were leaked.
If /etc/passwd or application config (.env) was accessed, check for subsequent unauthorized use of leaked credentials.
Block the source IP and verify web root directory traversal restrictions.

name: OS Command Injection Critical Response Runbook
immediate_actions: Assume potential Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the host.
Immediately isolate the affected host/container from the internal network.
Inspect running processes, network connections (netstat/ss), and cron jobs for reverse shells or backdoors.
Block the attacker IP and escalate to the Incident Response lead.

name: Automated Scanner and Reconnaissance Runbook
immediate_actions: Review the probe sequence to verify all requests received 403 or 404 responses.
Verify that no endpoints returned 200 OK with sensitive disclosures (e.g. phpinfo or .git).
If scanner persists beyond 100 requests: temporarily rate-limit or block the source IP.
If all probes failed and attack stopped, mark as low priority / monitored.
